'''Peter Kalmus''' (born May 9, 1974) is an American [[scientist]] and writer.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kalmus |first=Peter |date=2025-01-10 |title=Opinion {{!}} As a Climate Scientist, I Knew It Was Time to Leave Los Angeles |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/10/opinion/la-fires-los-angeles-wildfires.html |access-date=2025-01-11 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> He is a [[data scientist]] at [[NASA]]'s [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] as an associate project scientist at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]]'s Joint Institute for Regional Earth System Science & Engineering.

In addition to his scientific work, he is the author of the book, ''Being the Change: Live Well and Spark a Climate Revolution''.<ref name="kalmus-2017">
{{cite book
 | last1 = Kalmus | first1 = Peter
 | title = Being the change: live well and spark a climate revolution
 | date = July 10, 2017
| publisher = New Society Publishers
 | location = Gabriola Island, BC, Canada
 | isbn = 978-0-86571-853-1
}}  Paperback edition.
</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com.au/2017/06/25/why-this-nasa-jet-lab-scientist-will-never-go-near-a-jet-again_a_23001422/|title=Why This NASA Jet Lab Scientist Will Never Go Near A Jet Again|last=Sharwood|first=Anthony|date=June 27, 2017|work=Huffington Post|access-date=December 7, 2018|archive-date=November 17, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181117193857/https://www.huffingtonpost.com.au/2017/06/25/why-this-nasa-jet-lab-scientist-will-never-go-near-a-jet-again_a_23001422/|url-status=live}}</ref> A documentary by the same title complements the book.<ref>{{Citation|title=Being the Change: A New Kind of Climate Documentary (2018) - IMDb|url=http://www.imdb.com/title/tt8585080/plotsummary|access-date=September 15, 2019|archive-date=April 15, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220415045042/https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8585080/plotsummary|url-status=live}}</ref> In addition to authoring articles about [[climate change]], he is the founder of the website noflyclimatesci.org<ref name="no-fly-climate-sci">{{cite web
 | title = No Fly Climate Sci

 | url-status = live
 }}  Website.</ref> and co-founder of the [[Mobile app|app]], ''Earth Hero: Climate Change''.

== Education and early career ==
Kalmus attended [[Harvard University]], where he received his Bachelor of Science in physics in 1997.<ref name=":0"/>  At Harvard, he used [[Fourier-transform spectroscopy|Fourier-transform microwave spectroscopy]] to discover and categorize the quantum-mechanical rotational spectra of several [[cyanopolyyne]]s which were subsequently found in [[interstellar cloud]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Thaddeus|first1=P.|last2=Gottlieb|first2=C. == Research ==
After focusing on LIGO related work for several years, Kalmus's focus transitioned into earth and climate science.  Kalmus's recent research centers on [[cloud physics]], specifically improving basic understanding of [[Marine stratocumulus|marine stratocumulus clouds]]<ref name="Kalmus 9155–9170">{{Cite journal|last1=Kalmus|first1=Peter|last2=Lebsock|first2=Matthew|last3=Teixeira|first3=João|date=December 2014|title=Observational Boundary Layer Energy and Water Budgets of the Stratocumulus-to-Cumulus Transition|journal=Journal of Climate|volume=27|issue=24|pages=9155–9170|doi=10.1175/JCLI-D-14-00242.1|issn=0894-8755|bibcode=2014JCli...27.9155K|doi-access=free}}</ref> and severe convective weather such as [[tornado]]es<ref name="Kalmus 1633–1653">{{Cite journal|last1=Kalmus|first1=Peter|last2=Kahn|first2=Brian H.|last3=Freeman|first3=Sean W.|last4=van den Heever|first4=Susan C.|date=May 2019|title=Trajectory-Enhanced AIRS Observations of Environmental Factors Driving Severe Convective Storms|journal=Monthly Weather Review|volume=147|issue=5|pages=1633–1653|doi=10.1175/MWR-D-18-0055.1|issn=0027-0644|bibcode=2019MWRv..147.1633K|doi-access=free}}</ref> with the goal of improving projections of how these phenomena will change as the planet heats, using [[remote sensing]] data, ''in situ'' data, and models. Marine stratocumulus clouds reflect incoming sunlight, cooling the planet, and are difficult to model accurately in climate models; this makes them a major source of uncertainty in climate projections.<ref name="Kalmus 9155–9170"/>

A common thread in his research is improving the utility of satellite observations of the Earth. His work on severe weather unlocks the potential of polar orbiting satellites to observe rapidly changing convective environments by using air parcel trajectory modeling to span the temporal gap between satellite overpass and convective initiation.<ref name="Kalmus 1633–1653"/> He has used ''in situ'' data from a ship-based campaign to bias-correct the [[CloudSat]] warm rain retrieval. He also uses ''in situ'' data to validate retrievals from the AIRS instrument on the [[Aqua (satellite)]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kalmus|first1=Peter|last2=Sun Wong|last3=Teixeira|first3=Joao|date=July 2017|title=The Pacific Subtropical Cloud Transition: A MAGIC Assessment of AIRS and ECMWF Thermodynamic Structure|journal=IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters|volume=12|issue=7|pages=1586–1590|doi=10.1109/LGRS.2015.2413771|s2cid=8487808|issn=1545-598X}}</ref>

Kalmus also works in the nascent field of [[ecological forecasting]]. Coral reefs are rapidly succumbing to ocean heat waves and [[ocean acidification]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.climate.gov/news-features/featured-images/no-safe-haven-coral-combined-impacts-warming-and-ocean-acidification|title=No safe haven for coral from the combined impacts of warming and ocean acidification|website=www.climate.gov|access-date=August 1, 2019|archive-date=August 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801204123/https://www.climate.gov/news-features/featured-images/no-safe-haven-coral-combined-impacts-warming-and-ocean-acidification}}</ref> Kalmus is the principal investigator on a NASA grant to study the projected future of the world's coral reefs with improved accuracy and higher resolution.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cce.nasa.gov/cgi-bin/bio/pi_list.pl|title=Biological Diversity & Ecological Forecasting|website=cce.nasa.gov|access-date=August 1, 2019|archive-date=August 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801204125/https://cce.nasa.gov/cgi-bin/bio/pi_list.pl|url-status=live}}</ref> 

He has co-authored over 100 peer-reviewed scientific articles in physics and Earth science, with a majority having come from his previous participation in the LIGO Collaboration.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://publons.com/researcher/1915378/peter-kalmus/|title=Peter Kalmus' Publons profile|website=publons.com|access-date=August 1, 2019|archive-date=August 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801204124/https://publons.com/researcher/1915378/peter-kalmus/|url-status=live}}</ref>

often speaks to the need for an immediate and massive climate mobilization and how individuals can "vote" for this mobilization through their actions, via both activism and emissions reduction. He frequently speaks to the need for a [[carbon fee and dividend]] policy as part of the mobilization, in which fossil fuel becomes increasingly costly as the carbon fee rises every year and 100% of the net revenue is returned equitably to the people, making the policy fiscally progressive.{{Citation needed|date=August 2026}} He focuses in particular on encouraging the Earth science and other academic communities to speak out with greater urgency on the need for climate action.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kalmus|first=Peter|title=To My Fellow Climate Scientists: Be Human, Be Brave, Speak Truth|journal=Yes! Magazine|url=https://www.yesmagazine.org/issues/science/to-my-fellow-climate-scientists-be-human-be-brave-tell-the-truth-20170207|access-date=August 1, 2019|archive-date=August 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801204132/https://www.yesmagazine.org/issues/science/to-my-fellow-climate-scientists-be-human-be-brave-tell-the-truth-20170207|url-status=live}}</ref>

Kalmus' lifestyle uses approximately one-tenth the fossil fuel of the average American.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Being the Change: Live Well and Spark a Climate Revolution |last=Kalmus |first=Peter |publisher=New Society |year=2017 |page=144}}</ref> He says this has made his life more satisfying and meaningful. In 2010, Kalmus realized the flying in planes accounted for roughly {{frac|3|4}} of his greenhouse gas emissions, and he has not flown on a plane since 2012.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kalmus|first=Peter|title=How Far Can We Get Without Flying?|journal=Yes! Magazine|url=https://www.yesmagazine.org/issues/life-after-oil/how-far-can-we-get-without-flying-20160211|access-date=August 1, 2019|archive-date=August 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801204123/https://www.yesmagazine.org/issues/life-after-oil/how-far-can-we-get-without-flying-20160211|url-status=live}}</ref> Kalmus believes that anyone can contribute to cultural shift by conspicuously modeling the change that needs to happen. He has stated that by "walking the talk" his advocacy has become more effective.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theweek.com/articles/783575/whats-most-effective-way-talk-about-climate-change|title=What's the most effective way to talk about climate change?|date=July 15, 2018|website=theweek.com|access-date=August 1, 2019|archive-date=August 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801204123/https://theweek.com/articles/783575/whats-most-effective-way-talk-about-climate-change|url-status=live}}</ref> Kalmus' book, ''Being the Change'', addresses climate change and the changes individuals can make in their lifestyle.

Kalmus is a columnist and regular contributor at [[Yes! (U.S. magazine)|''YES!'' magazine]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Peter Kalmus|url=https://www.yesmagazine.org/authors/peter-kalmus|access-date=August 20, 2021|website=YES! Magazine|language=en-US|archive-date=August 20, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210820231249/https://www.yesmagazine.org/authors/peter-kalmus|url-status=live}}</ref> His writing has also appeared in ''[[The Guardian]]'',<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2017/dec/11/climate-scientists-emit-30000-tonnes-c02|title=Why did climate scientists emit 30,000 tonnes of CO2 this weekend? {{!}} Peter Kalmus|last=Kalmus|first=Peter|date=December 11, 2017|work=The Guardian|access-date=August 1, 2019|issn=0261-3077|archive-date=July 28, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190728144101/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2017/dec/11/climate-scientists-emit-30000-tonnes-c02|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Eos (magazine)|''Eos'']], ''[[The Washington Post]]'', and [[Grist (magazine)|''Grist'']].

On September 14, 2019, Kalmus tweeted "Never give up" and referenced his latest article, "How to live with the climate crisis without becoming a nihilist".<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/opinion/story/2019-09-13/global-warming-climate-change-science-activism-jonathan-franzen|title=Opinion: How to live with the climate crisis without becoming a nihilist|date=September 15, 2019|website=Los Angeles Times|language=en-US|access-date=September 15, 2019|archive-date=September 15, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190915035446/https://www.latimes.com/opinion/story/2019-09-13/global-warming-climate-change-science-activism-jonathan-franzen|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mobile.twitter.com/ClimateHuman/status/1172925005098704896|title=Twitter|website=mobile.twitter.com|access-date=September 15, 2019|archive-date=April 22, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220422123008/https://mobile.twitter.com/ClimateHuman/status/1172925005098704896|url-status=live}}</ref>

Kalmus has been associated with the [[Movement for a People's Party]], a progressive organization positioned as an alternative to the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] or [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]]. After the first presidential [[2020 United States presidential debates|debate]] of the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 election]], Kalmus participated in a four-person response to the debate.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Movement For A People's Party - A Party For Us|url=https://peoplesparty.org/|access-date=October 12, 2020|website=The People's Party|language=en-US|archive-date=August 17, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200817223601/https://peoplesparty.org/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In late{{nbhyph}}2021, Kalmus likened his own experiences pushing for greater recognition of the climate problem with those of the two fictional [[astronomer]]s portrayed in the comedy film [[Don't Look Up (2021 film)|''Don't Look Up'']].  He also compares absurd events in that film with a series of equally absurd and elusory events in our own world.<ref name="kalmus-2021">{{cite news

 }}</ref>

Kalmus, along with other climate activists, chained himself to the main doors of the [[Charlotte Douglas International Airport]] private jet terminal on November 10, 2022. He was charged with trespassing.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Boraks |first1=David |title=These climate scientists feel 'a higher calling' — civil disobedience |url=https://www.wfae.org/energy-environment/2022-11-11/these-climate-scientists-feel-a-higher-calling-civil-disobedience |work=WFAE 90.7 |date=November 11, 2022 |language=en |access-date=November 14, 2022 |archive-date=November 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221114063146/https://www.wfae.org/energy-environment/2022-11-11/these-climate-scientists-feel-a-higher-calling-civil-disobedience |url-status=live }}</ref>

In December 2022, Kalmus and climate scientist Rose Abramoff briefly showed a banner at the eve of a plenary session of the [[American Geophysical Union]]'s annual Fall Meeting with a call for scientists to engage in protest against climate change: " ''Out of the lab and into the streets »'' . AGU removed their research presentations from the meeting, banned them from participation, launched a misconduct inquiry, and complained to Abramoff's employer, [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]]. Kalmus and Abramoff further claimed that AGU threatened to have them arrested if they returned to the meeting.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McFall-Johnsen |first1=Morgan |title=2 climate activists got kicked out of the world's biggest Earth-science conference for protesting, and one says the association is 'silencing scientists' |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/climate-researchers-ejected-from-agu-fall-meeting-banner-activism-interview-2022-12 |access-date=January 11, 2023 |work=Business Insider |date=December 16, 2022 |archive-date=January 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230110173730/https://www.businessinsider.com/climate-researchers-ejected-from-agu-fall-meeting-banner-activism-interview-2022-12 |url-status=live }}</ref> Abramoff was subsequently fired by Oak Ridge.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Abramoff |first1=Rose |title=I'm a Scientist Who Spoke Up About Climate Change. My Employer Fired Me. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/01/10/opinion/scientist-fired-climate-change-activism.html |access-date=January 11, 2023 |work=The New York Times |date=January 10, 2023 |archive-date=January 11, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230111003522/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/01/10/opinion/scientist-fired-climate-change-activism.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In January 2023, 1500 scientists signed an appeal to object to what happened to their colleagues.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-01-26 |title=Civil disobedience: 'Climate scientists are citizens and humans too' |language=en |work=Le Monde.fr |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/opinion/article/2023/01/26/civil-disobedience-climate-scientists-are-citizens-and-humans-too_6013152_23.html |access-date=2023-01-27}}</ref>

=== JP Morgan Chase building arrest ===
On April 6, 2022, Kalmus was arrested, along with a physicist, an engineer and a science teacher,<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 7, 2022 |title=Climate Scientists Chained Themselves To A Downtown Bank's Doors In An Act Of Peaceful Protest. Police In Riot Gear Shut It Down |url=https://laist.com/news/climate-environment/climate-revolution-now-how-an-atypical-scientific-protest-led-to-arrests-in-dtla |access-date=April 20, 2022 |website=LAist |language=en |archive-date=April 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220420142532/https://laist.com/news/climate-environment/climate-revolution-now-how-an-atypical-scientific-protest-led-to-arrests-in-dtla |url-status=live }}</ref> for chaining himself to the door of the [[JP Morgan Chase]] building in Los Angeles, protesting the bank's investments in new fossil fuel projects.<ref name="kalmus-2022">{{cite news
 | last1 = Kalmus
 | first1 = Peter
 | title = Climate scientists are desperate: we're crying, begging and getting arrested
 | date = April 6, 2022
 | work = The Guardian
 | location = London, United Kingdom
 | issn = 0261-3077
 | url = https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2022/apr/06/climate-scientists-are-desperate-were-crying-begging-and-getting-arrested
 | access-date = April 6, 2022
 | archive-date = April 6, 2022
 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220406202121/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2022/apr/06/climate-scientists-are-desperate-were-crying-begging-and-getting-arrested
 | url-status = live
 }}</ref> Writing in ''[[The Guardian]]'' in April{{nbsp}}2022, Kalmus advocated [[civil disobedience]] following the release of the final IPCC Working Group III report.  In the article, Kalmus says "It's now the eleventh hour and I feel terrified for my kids, and terrified for humanity. [...] But I'll keep fighting as hard as I can for this Earth, no matter how bad it gets, because it can always get worse".<ref name="kalmus-2022" />

=== Flying Less movement ===
Kalmus is the founder of the website noflyclimatesci.org and a leading voice in the #FlyingLess movement.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://noflyclimatesci.org/|title=Welcome|last=Sci|first=No Fly Climate|website=Earth scientists flying less|access-date=August 1, 2019|archive-date=August 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801204126/https://noflyclimatesci.org/|url-status=live}}</ref> He is pushing for the [[American Geophysical Union]] to support earth scientists who choose to fly less out of climate concerns, with remote participation options at conferences.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eos.org/opinions/agu-should-support-its-members-who-fly-less|title=AGU Should Support Its Members Who Fly Less|website=Eos|date=December 7, 2018|access-date=August 1, 2019|archive-date=August 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801204124/https://eos.org/opinions/agu-should-support-its-members-who-fly-less|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== School strike for climate ===
Kalmus was a lead organizer on two letters written in support of school striking youth, one from US Earth scientists<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/observations/an-open-letter-endorsing-the-global-school-strike-for-climate/|title=An Open Letter Endorsing the Global School Strike for Climate|last=Lemonick|first=Michael D.|website=Scientific American Blog Network|access-date=August 1, 2019|archive-date=January 18, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230118131806/https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/observations/an-open-letter-endorsing-the-global-school-strike-for-climate/|url-status=live}}</ref> and one from international scholars.<ref name="hagedorn-etal-2019">
{{cite journal

</ref>  His two sons have been regularly school striking on Fridays since 2018 as part of the [[School strike for climate|Fridays for Future movement]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eos.org/articles/youth-call-for-action-with-climate-strikes|title=Youth Call for Action with Climate Strikes|website=EosS|date=March 14, 2019|access-date=August 1, 2019|archive-date=September 24, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190924064646/https://eos.org/articles/youth-call-for-action-with-climate-strikes|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Earth Hero ===
To help users track carbon emissions, Kalmus co-founded the [[mobile app|smart phone app]] ''Earth Hero''. It aims to help users reduce their emissions, shift culture with their reductions, and engage in other forms of climate activism such as protest and civil disobedience.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.earthhero.org/|title=Earth Hero|website=Earth Hero|access-date=August 1, 2019|archive-date=August 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801204125/https://www.earthhero.org/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
Kalmus has won numerous awards both for his science and activism. He received the [[NASA Early Career Achievement Medal]] and three Jet Propulsion Laboratory Voyager Awards for his work in Earth science.<ref name=":0" /> He is also a recipient of the inaugural [[Transition town|Transition]] US Walking the Talk award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.transitionus.org/blog/transition-us-awards-ceremony-honors-movement-leaders|title=Transition US Awards Ceremony Honors Movement Leaders {{!}} Transition US|website=www.transitionus.org|access-date=August 1, 2019|archive-date=August 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801204133/https://www.transitionus.org/blog/transition-us-awards-ceremony-honors-movement-leaders|url-status=live}}</ref> He is a 2018 "Grist 50" fellow, one of the ten 2018 fellows classified as "Visionaries".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://grist.org/grist-50/2018/|title=Meet the people fixing your world|website=Grist|access-date=August 1, 2019|archive-date=August 9, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190809013618/https://grist.org/grist-50/2018/|url-status=live}}</ref>

His book, ''Being the Change: Live Well and Spark a Climate Revolution,'' won an [[Independent Publisher Book Awards|IPPY]] Outstanding Book of the Year Award,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ippyawards.com/129/medalists/2018-medalists-categories-1-42/outstanding|title=Outstanding|website=www.ippyawards.com|access-date=December 6, 2018|archive-date=October 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006202803/http://www.ippyawards.com/129/medalists/2018-medalists-categories-1-42/outstanding|url-status=live}}</ref> the [[Nautilus Book Awards|Nautilus Book Award]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Past Winners |url=https://www.nautilusbookawards.com/nautilus-past-winners |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=Nautilus Book Awards |language=en}}</ref> and the Foreword Indies Book Award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Full List of 2017 Foreword INDIES Winners |url=https://www.forewordreviews.com/awards/winners/2017/ |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=www.forewordreviews.com |language=en}}</ref>
